subject.title: Teams: local multi-user Workspaces sharing with exact tab RBAC

question: Should OpenClaw own a first-party gateway-local multi-user Teams product, or only expose generic identity and exact-resource authorization seams for a Workspaces-owned implementation?
rationale: The proposal changes stable gateway authentication and plugin SDK contracts while crossing the recently established Workspaces ownership boundary; repository evidence cannot decide that permanent product commitment.

options.title: Generic seams plus Workspaces
options.body: Sponsor only reusable core identity and resource-authorization primitives, with Teams-specific invitations, grants, approvals, and portal behavior owned by Workspaces.

options.title: First-party Teams core
options.body: Sponsor the complete cross-cutting Teams product with staged threat-model, compatibility, migration, and portal-isolation review.

options.title: Decline multi-user sharing
options.body: Keep the gateway operator-oriented and do not add this product surface.

recommendation.title: Generic seams plus Workspaces
recommendation.body: Sponsor only reusable core identity and resource-authorization primitives, with Teams-specific invitations, grants, approvals, and portal behavior owned by Workspaces.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the current Workspaces foundation and its explicit plugin/core product boundary.
